title: The path exemption of the closed-value rule passes any slash-bearing secret value that prose closes with a comma or bracket
goal: kbpublic.file_hits flags an unquoted assignment whose value is a mixed-case base64-style string holding slashes and is followed by , ) ] }, while a lower-case path such as kb/public/x.md and a snake_case code name stay unflagged when so closed

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbpublic as p;v='wJalrXUtnFEM'+'I/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCY';k='sec'+'ret=';ts=[k+v+',','('+k+v+')','the '+k[:-1]+': '+v+', then'];r=[bool([h for h in p.file_hits('kb/public/x.md',t,{}) if h[0]=='secret']) for t in ts];print(r);sys.exit(0 if all(r) else 1)

gates.question: Which values does the closed-value rule still read as a path reference: a value with a slash whose parts are all lower-case, or any slash value?
options: A lower-case path with a slash, and any value with a backslash, as before
A path with a slash whose parts are all lower-case only, a backslash path flagged too
gates.recommendation: A lower-case path with a slash, and any value with a backslash, as before
gates.answer: A lower-case path with a slash, and any value with a backslash, as before

notes: The review also found kb/_self/git.md:119 still defines a placeholder value as 'a code character' and nothing in kb/_self says the closed-value reading (closing , ) ] } and a code span's backticks stripped first; a snake_case name or path so closed is a reference) or the EC armor-label exemptions (camel-case path piece, lower-camel or digit identifier cell). Whoever lands the last of the two items edits git.md and names plugin.md and tools.md only if they change.
